summary: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF) Overseas Scholarship Scheme pays for Nigerians to do an MSc or PhD at partner universities in the UK, Germany, France or Malaysia, in fields that serve the oil and gas sector. It covers return flights, tuition and bench fees, health insurance and living allowances. Winners have strong O'Level and degree results, a course clearly linked to the petroleum industry, professional-body membership and a sharp statement of purpose or proposal, and they perform well at the screening interview.
lookfor: Strong academic record: 2:1 (or 2:2 plus industry experience) for MSc; at least 2:2 plus a good master's for PhD
Strong O'Level results: five credits including English and Mathematics
A statement of purpose (MSc) or research proposal (PhD) that fits the needs of Nigeria's oil and gas industry
Membership of a relevant professional body
Performance at the screening interview and clean, verifiable documents
Final list balanced across the 36 states and FCT (federal character)
cycle: 2026/27 round closed 27 Feb 2026; 38,398 applied, 5,885 were screened in six zones on 7-17 April 2026. The next round (for 2027/28) usually opens in January and runs about six weeks, so expect roughly mid-January to late February 2027 - check the current guidance.

eligibility.q: Are you a Nigerian citizen with a verified National Identity Number (NIN)?
eligibility.no: PTDF is only for Nigerians. Enrol for NIN at any NIMC centre now - the portal checks it. Non-Nigerians should look at Commonwealth, Chevening or DAAD awards instead.

eligibility.q: Have you completed NYSC (discharge certificate) or do you have an exemption letter?
eligibility.no: You cannot apply until NYSC is finished. Plan for the round after your passing-out, and use the waiting time to join a professional body and draft your statement.

eligibility.q: Do you have five O'Level credits including English and Mathematics?
eligibility.no: PTDF will not accept you without them. Consider resitting WAEC/NECO, or look at awards that do not screen O'Levels.

eligibility.q: MSc: do you have at least a 2:1, or a 2:2 plus relevant industry experience? PhD: at least a 2:2 first degree and a strong master's?
eligibility.no: Gain relevant industry experience (2:2 holders) or complete a local master's first; the PTDF In-Country Scholarship and NNPC/TotalEnergies are other options.

eligibility.q: Is your planned course or research clearly relevant to the oil and gas sector (engineering, geosciences, environment, energy, petroleum economics, management or law)?
eligibility.no: PTDF only funds petroleum-related study. If your field is unrelated, look at Chevening, Commonwealth or DAAD instead.

eligibility.q: Have you never held a PTDF scholarship at the same or a lower level, and are you not holding another scholarship now?
eligibility.no: Past PTDF scholars cannot apply for the same or lower level. Lecturers need their Vice-Chancellor to confirm they hold no other current scholarship.

steps.title: Confirm you meet every PTDF rule
steps.why: Thousands are dropped at the first screen for one missing rule. Ten minutes of checking saves weeks of wasted work.
do: Open the PTDF guidelines page and read every eligibility line for your level (MSc or PhD).
Write each rule on paper and tick it only if you have the document to prove it today.
Check your NIN details match the name on your degree, WAEC and NYSC certificates.
If you are a lecturer, ask your university how to get the Vice-Chancellor's 'no other scholarship' confirmation.
tips: Read the official guidelines, not blog copies - blogs often mix up the Overseas and In-Country schemes.
avoid: Applying for both MSc and PhD - multiple applications lead to automatic disqualification.
check: I can say yes to every 'must' rule and have proof for each one.

steps.title: Understand how PTDF picks winners
steps.why: PTDF shortlists by documents, then decides by screening interview. Knowing this tells you where to spend your effort.
do: Note the selection path: online application, paper screen, invitation to a zonal interview and document check, final list by state.
Read a news report of the April 2026 screening to see the scale (over 38,000 applicants, about 5,885 screened).
List the four things officials said they look at: strong O'Level, proposal or statement, professional-body membership, fit with industry needs.
Rate yourself honestly on each one and write down what you will improve before the next round.
tips: Competition is per state. You compete mostly with people from your own state of origin, so your LGA letter matters.
avoid: Thinking a first-class degree alone wins - the interview decides.
check: I know which of the four strengths is my weakest and have a plan for it.

steps.title: Choose your course, country and backup awards
steps.why: Your course must be clearly useful to the petroleum industry. A focused choice also makes your statement much stronger.
do: Write one sentence: 'I want to study X because Nigeria's oil and gas sector needs Y.'
Pick 2-3 course titles that match (e.g. petroleum engineering, reservoir geoscience, environmental management for oil and gas, energy economics, petroleum law).

Decide on country: UK, Germany, France or Malaysia. PhD applicants: note that UK PhDs are split-site with the College of Petroleum and Energy Studies, Kaduna and Robert Gordon, Strathclyde or Portsmouth.
Note backups: PTDF In-Country Scholarship (Nigerian public universities, usually April-June), NNPC/TotalEnergies Master's (France), Chevening, Commonwealth.
tips: The 2026/27 overseas advert did not list an admission letter. PTDF places scholars with its partner universities - check the current guidance before paying any application fees elsewhere.
avoid: Choosing a course with no clear oil and gas link, such as general business or pure computer science.
check: I can explain in one sentence how my course serves the petroleum sector.

steps.title: Build your timeline and watch for the advert
steps.why: The window is short (about six weeks) and the portal slows near the deadline. Starting early is the easiest advantage you can get.
do: Put 'PTDF opens - check' in your calendar for early January 2027 and set a weekly reminder from December.
Work backwards from late February: documents ready by early January, statement final by end of January, submit in the first two weeks.
Bookmark ptdf.gov.ng and the scholarship portal. Only trust adverts on .gov.ng sites or major newspapers.
Create a folder on your phone and laptop called 'PTDF 2027' for scans.
tips: Follow PTDF's official channels; news agencies such as NAN repeat their notices.
avoid: Paying anyone for 'forms', 'slots' or 'shortlist help'. PTDF applications are free.
check: I have dates in my calendar and a folder ready.

steps.title: Fix name mismatches and verify your NIN
steps.why: At the screening, officers compare every document. A different spelling or missing middle name can end your chance.
do: Lay out your WAEC/NECO, degree certificate, NYSC certificate, birth certificate and NIN slip side by side.
If names differ, swear an affidavit at a High Court registry and publish a change-of-name notice if needed.
If your NIN details are wrong, book a data modification at a NIMC office (allow several weeks).
Scan the affidavit and keep the original for interview day.
tips: Start this first - government offices are slow in December and January.
avoid: Leaving NIN corrections until the portal rejects you.
check: My name is identical (or explained by affidavit) on every document.

steps.title: Collect academic documents and result PINs
steps.why: Degree certificates and transcripts from Nigerian universities can take months. Your WAEC/NECO results must come with a checker PIN.
do: Request your degree certificate from your university's Academic Office; if not ready, get a signed statement of result.
Buy a WAEC or NECO result-checker PIN (scratch card or the exam body's online store) for each sitting you will use.
PhD applicants: get your master's certificate or statement of result and transcript.
Scan each document in colour as a clear PDF, named e.g. 'Surname_Degree.pdf'.
tips: Do not use the PIN to check results yourself until you know how many uses it allows - you may need it for PTDF.
avoid: Uploading phone photos with shadows or cut-off edges.
check: I have clear scans of first degree, O'Level results plus PIN, and (PhD) master's.

links.t: Watch: Scholar Application Requirement Checklist/Your Best Recipe for Most Applications (Via Scholaris)

steps.title: Get NYSC, LGA letter and passport photo ready
steps.why: These prove you are eligible and which state you compete in. Missing ones are a common reason for failing the document check.
do: Find your NYSC discharge or exemption certificate. If lost, start the replacement process with NYSC now.
Visit your Local Government secretariat and request an LGA identification (indigene) letter on letterhead, signed and stamped.
Take a recent passport photograph on a white background and save a digital copy.
Scan all three clearly.
tips: Ask the LGA for two originals - you will need one at the screening.
avoid: Using a state-of-residence letter instead of your LGA of origin letter.
check: I have NYSC, LGA letter and photo scanned and the originals safe.

steps.title: Join a relevant professional body
steps.why: Officials list professional-body membership as one of the things they weigh. Many applicants skip it.
do: Pick the body for your field, for example Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE), COREN graduate registration, Society of Petroleum Engineers (SPE), Nigerian Association of Petroleum Explorationists (NAPE), Nigerian Mining and Geosciences Society, or Nigerian Environmental Society.
Apply for student, graduate or associate membership and pay the dues.
Ask for a membership certificate or letter and scan it.
Attend at least one chapter event so you can talk about it at interview.
tips: Join early - some bodies take weeks to issue certificates.
avoid: Listing a membership you cannot prove with a document.
check: I have a dated membership document from a relevant body.

links.t: Watch: Membership of Professional Bodies (Via Scholaris)

steps.title: MSc: write your statement of purpose
steps.why: For MSc applicants this is the main place you show why PTDF should invest in you.
do: Paragraph 1: the problem in Nigeria's oil and gas sector you want to help solve (one concrete example).
Paragraph 2: your background - degree, NYSC, work or project that connects to it.
Paragraph 3: the course you want and what you will learn that you cannot easily learn now.
Paragraph 4: your plan after study - the role you will take in Nigeria and the change you will make.
Cut to 500 words or fewer and have someone in the industry read it.
tips: Use numbers and names: a field, a process, a policy, a company type.
Show you will return - PTDF funds people who will come back and serve Nigeria's industry.
avoid: Generic lines like 'I have always been passionate about oil and gas'.
Copying online samples - interviewers ask about what you wrote.
check: Every paragraph links back to Nigeria's petroleum industry.

links.t: Watch: How to Write a Good Statement of Purpose for the PTDF Scholarship (Via Scholaris)

steps.prompt: Why you want the course, how it is relevant to the oil and gas industry, and how you will contribute to national development.

steps.title: PhD: write your oil and gas research proposal
steps.why: For PhD applicants the proposal is judged directly and discussed at the interview.
do: Use these headings: Title; Background and problem; Aim and objectives; Methodology; Data collection; Expected outcomes and relevance to Nigeria's oil and gas industry; References.
Keep objectives to 3-4 measurable items.
Say exactly what data you will collect, where, and how you will analyse it.
Ask a lecturer with a PhD to review it and correct gaps.
Keep it to five pages or fewer.
tips: Tie the problem to a real Nigerian context (e.g. gas flaring, produced water, local refining, Niger Delta remediation).
avoid: Over-ambitious topics that need equipment or data you cannot get.
check: A non-expert can understand the problem in the first half page.
It is five pages or fewer.

links.t: Watch: Writing an Award-Winning PhD Research Proposal for the PTDF Scholarship (Via Scholaris)

steps.prompt: A research proposal relevant to the oil and gas industry covering topic, background, objectives, methodology and data collection.

steps.title: Line up two referees for later
steps.why: The 2026/27 PTDF form did not list reference letters, but partner universities will ask for them once you are placed. Being ready saves weeks.
do: Choose two people: a lecturer who taught or supervised you, and a work or NYSC supervisor.
Message each one, explain PTDF and ask if they will write a reference later.
Send them your CV and draft statement or proposal.
Save their full names, titles, official emails and phone numbers.
tips: Use official email addresses; universities often reject Gmail references.
avoid: Choosing a famous person who barely knows you.
check: Two referees have agreed and I have their details.

steps.title: Create your portal account and fill the form
steps.why: A careful, complete form gets you through the first screen.
do: Go to scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng and register with an email and phone you will keep for a year.
Select the Overseas Scholarship Scheme and your level (MSc or PhD).
Enter personal data exactly as on your NIN.
Enter O'Level, degree and NYSC details, then upload each scanned document in the right box.
Paste in your statement of purpose or upload your proposal.
tips: Fill the form on a laptop with good internet early in the morning when the portal is fast.
avoid: Creating two accounts - it can be treated as a multiple application.
check: Every section shows complete and every upload opens correctly.

steps.title: Proofread, submit early and save proof
steps.why: Falsified or wrong details lead to disqualification, and late-week portal jams lock people out.
do: Print or download a preview and read every field aloud.
Ask a friend to check your name, dates and grades against your certificates.
Submit at least a week before the deadline.
Download or screenshot the confirmation and save the email.
tips: Keep your login details in a safe place - you will need them to check shortlist status.
check: I have a saved submission confirmation.

links.t: Watch: Blunders that can Ruin your Scholarship Application (Via Scholaris)

steps.title: Watch for the shortlist and invitation
steps.why: Shortlisted candidates are contacted with time and venue. Missing the message means missing the interview.
do: Check your email (including spam), SMS and the portal weekly from March.
When invited, note the centre: interviews run in the six zones (2026: Abuja, Bauchi, Kaduna, Rivers, Enugu, Oyo).
Plan transport and lodging - interviews were held over about ten days in April 2026.
Print the invitation.
tips: Check PTDF's website and major news agencies for shortlist notices in case an email fails.
avoid: Trusting WhatsApp 'shortlists' that ask for money.
check: I know my date, time and venue.

steps.title: Prepare for the screening interview
steps.why: In past rounds PTDF stated that selection is based strictly on interview performance, alongside document verification.
do: Pack originals and two photocopies of every document you uploaded, plus passport photos and your invitation.
Re-read your statement or proposal and prepare a one-minute summary.
Practise answers: Why this course? How does it help Nigeria's oil and gas sector? What will you do after? Explain your proposal's method.
Read current Nigerian energy news (e.g. the Petroleum Industry Act, gas flaring, refining).
Dress formally and arrive early.
tips: Practise aloud with a friend timing you; keep each answer under two minutes.
avoid: Arriving without originals - document verification happens on the day.
check: I can explain my course and its value to Nigeria without notes.

steps.title: Accept the award and prepare to travel
steps.why: Final lists depend on budget and federal character. Once selected, placement, bond and visa steps follow quickly.
do: Watch the PTDF website for the successful list and follow the acceptance instructions exactly.
Complete placement or admission steps with the partner university PTDF assigns.
Read the award terms carefully, including any bond or undertaking to return to Nigeria, before signing.
Get or renew your international passport and start the visa process as soon as you have an offer.
If not selected, ask for feedback where possible and prepare for the next January round.
tips: Keep paying close attention to official email - deadlines for acceptance can be short.
avoid: Resigning from your job before you have a written award letter and visa.
check: I have a written award, a placement and a visa plan.

faq.q: Do I need an admission letter before applying for the overseas scheme?
faq.a: The 2026/27 overseas announcement did not list one; PTDF places scholars at its partner universities. Check the current guidance. The In-Country scheme does require admission to a Nigerian public university.
No. Applying is free on scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng. Do not pay anyone for forms or slots.
For MSc, only with relevant industry experience. For PhD, a 2:2 first degree is the minimum, alongside a strong master's.

faq.q: What if I miss the January-February window?
faq.a: Prepare for the next year's round, and consider the PTDF In-Country Scholarship, which opened 27 April - 5 June in 2026.
Yes. Final selection follows federal character, so you mainly compete with applicants from your state of origin.
